extracted.intended_audience: cosmetic industry stakeholders (manufacturers, processors), regulatory affairs professionals, FDA staff, and public commenters on MoCRA implementation
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts and summarizes the substantive regulatory requirements, guidance topics, and implementation criteria the FDA has published under the Modernization of Cosmetics Regulation Act (MoCRA) for facility registration, product listing, testing, records access, recalls, labeling, adverse event reporting, and related agency processes. Useful for industry compliance and for preparing notice-and-comment submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facility registration requirement (Section 607(a) of FD&C Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 607(a) of the FD&C Act (21 U.S.C. 364c(a)) requires every person that owns or operates a facility that engages in the manufacturing or processing of a cosmetic product for distribution in the United States to register each facility with FDA no later than one year after the date of enactment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance documents (Registration and Listing of Cosmetic Product Facilities and Products) are intended to assist persons submitting cosmetic product facility registrations. The guidance includes explanations and FAQs (Appendix B) to clarify who must register, timing, and how registrations are submitted (including transition from prior voluntary systems).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cosmetic product listing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: MoCRA added statutory requirements for cosmetic product listing submissions to FDA; affected persons must submit product listing information as specified by the statute and implementing guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Registration and Listing guidance and its Appendix B provide details and FAQs about product listing submissions, what information to include, and how to submit entries via the planned electronic submission portal or interim mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and Listing guidance content and FAQs (Appendix B)
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA published 'Registration and Listing of Cosmetic Product Facilities and Products; Guidance for Industry' that finalizes prior draft guidance and includes a set of frequently asked questions and answers (Appendix B) to explain FDA's current thinking on facility registration and product listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance clarifies submission expectations, contains three new draft FAQs for comment (in the latest version), and includes minor clarifying edits. It is intended to assist persons submitting registrations and product listings under MoCRA and explains interpretation and implementation issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submissions portal and pilot program (User Acceptance Testing)
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA is implementing an electronic submissions portal for cosmetic product facility registration and product listing pursuant to MoCRA and is soliciting participants for a voluntary pilot program to conduct user acceptance testing (UAT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCAC and OCS plan to accept up to nine participants to provide input to evaluate the portal. The pilot is voluntary and intended to inform development and usability of the electronic submission system; guidance documents reference the portal as the expected mechanism for submissions once implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing methods for detecting and identifying asbestos in talc-containing cosmetic products (proposed rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA proposed to require testing of talc-containing cosmetic products using standardized testing methods for detecting and identifying asbestos that may be present as a contaminant in talc; the proposed rule includes corresponding adulteration provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rule would require manufacturers of talc-containing cosmetic products to test their finished products or the talc cosmetic ingredient prior to using the talc. The preamble notes asbestos is a potential contaminant and a known human carcinogen, and that even low levels in cosmetics applied to the body may render the product injurious. (Note: FDA later announced withdrawal of an iteration of this proposed rule in response to comments warranting further consideration.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Adulteration standard tied to asbestos testing
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA proposes adulteration provisions related to asbestos in talc-containing cosmetics — presence of asbestos may render a cosmetic injurious and therefore adulterated under statutory standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed rule links required standardized testing to adulteration determinations and potential regulatory actions (e.g., recalls, enforcement) if asbestos is detected.

rubrics_metrics.name: FDA records access authority for cosmetics (Sections 605 and 610; amended section 704(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: MoCRA added sections 605 (21 U.S.C. 364a) and 610 (21 U.S.C. 364f) to, and amended section 704(a)(1) (21 U.S.C. 374(a)(1)) of, the FD&C Act, establishing new authorities for FDA to access and copy records related to cosmetic products for inspection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The draft guidance 'FDA Records Access Authority for Cosmetics' provides answers to FAQs about the criteria, process, and expectations for FDA's access to and copying of cosmetic-related records, explaining agency current thinking and how those authorities may be exercised during inspections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory cosmetics recalls implementation (Section 611)
rubrics_metrics.description: MoCRA added mandatory cosmetics recall authority (section 611 of the FD&C Act). FDA published a draft Q&A guidance titled 'Questions and Answers Regarding Mandatory Cosmetics Recalls' to explain implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The draft guidance provides answers to common questions about FDA's mandatory recall authority, including criteria for initiating a mandatory recall, the administrative/process steps, expectations for industry, and how FDA will exercise this authority when finalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of Good Manufacturing Practices (GMPs) for cosmetic products
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA is conducting stakeholder outreach (listening sessions) to inform efforts to develop regulations that would establish good manufacturing practices for facilities that manufacture or process cosmetic products distributed in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listening sessions solicit input from manufacturers (including small businesses), consumer organizations, and experts about how manufacturing practices impact the likelihood of adverse events, differences by product type, and practical considerations for drafting GMP regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cosmetic labeling requirements and related information collection (PRA notices)
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA is soliciting public comment under the Paperwork Reduction Act on proposed collections to support implementation of cosmetic labeling regulations and new statutory provisions for labeling, facility registration, and product listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices identify OMB control numbers and request comments on burden estimates and information collection instruments associated with labeling regulations and MoCRA-required submissions; comments will inform final PRA submissions and paperwork estimates used in rulemaking and guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adverse event and product experience reporting program revisions to include cosmetics
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA is revising its Adverse Event and Product Experience Reporting Program instructions to incorporate cosmetics: e.g., adding text ', or cosmetic product' in form instructions, removing ambiguous conjunctions, and specifying which sections to fill when reporting ONLY a cosmetic product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The instructional supplement details form field changes and routing for cosmetic-only reports (which sections to fill), ensuring adverse events involving cosmetics are reported and processed appropriately under the Agency's reporting system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance policy on enforcement timing (enforcement delay)
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA published a 'Compliance Policy for Cosmetic Product Facility Registration and Cosmetic Product Listing' guidance announcing the Agency's intention to delay enforcement of registration and listing requirements for an additional six months after the initial December 29, 2023, deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This compliance policy guidance explains enforcement discretion timelines and provides industry with information about when FDA expects to begin enforcing MoCRA registration and listing requirements, giving regulated entities additional time to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of public comments and administrative processes in rule development
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Register notices record that agency actions (e.g., withdrawing a proposed rule on asbestos testing) can be influenced by comments received during the comment period that warrant further consideration and assessment prior to issuing final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholder comments on proposed rules and draft guidance materially affect rulemaking trajectories; agencies may withdraw, revise, or delay rules in response to substantive comments. Notices often invite further public input and participation in pilot programs and listening sessions to shape final policies.
